state.decision: How GrapiX should represent and render an animated Bezier path (a shape's path or a mask's path whose vertices and handles move over time).
state.what_exists_today: A path is BezierPath {closed, vertices, in_tangents, out_tangents} (handles are offsets). A scene's timeline holds only numeric KeyframeChannel {object_id, property, keys[{frame, value, easing}]}; Auto-Key, easing, the speed graph and the keyframe editor all work on those numeric channels. Edits to a path are one editPath edit (insert, delete, convert, move, set handle, reshape, reverse, set first vertex, join, keep-shape delete). The GPU compositor draws a shape's layer source ONCE at prepare into a texture; the frame path only changes transforms, opacity and effect parameters. Animated width or height is already refused by name for the GPU engine (it needs a GPU source backend); the CPU reference renders everything per frame.
state.requirements_from_the_specs: Pen and Masking specs v2: a stable anchor id per vertex across keyframes; inserting a vertex on an animated path splits the curve exactly (De Casteljau) in EVERY keyframe so the shape at each key is unchanged; deleting follows a stated policy; Set First Vertex is explicit; a key with a different topology must hold, never interpolate by index; one drag is one undo step; editor and playout must evaluate the same geometry at the same frame.

options.A: A path channel in the timeline: {object_id, target (shape subpath or mask index), keys[{frame, path, easing}]}. Each key holds a whole BezierPath carrying stable vertex ids. Interpolation is per vertex id between neighbouring keys of equal topology; a topology mismatch holds the earlier key. An insert edits every key.
options.B: Per-vertex numeric channels in the existing timeline: properties like path.<vertexId>.x, .y, .inX, .inY, .outX, .outY (six per vertex), reusing the numeric keyframe machinery, easing, Auto-Key and editor.
options.C: Do not animate paths; offer morphs only as an effect or a trim.

state.rendering_note: Either A or B needs the shape source redrawn per frame. A proposed way: size the layer source texture once to the union of all keys' bounds, and redraw into that same texture each frame the path changes (Vello GPU, bounded to animated shapes); the CPU reference re-prepares the animated layer each frame.

best_representation.instructions: Which representation should GrapiX adopt for animated paths?

criteria.A: Option A: a path channel whose keys are whole paths with stable vertex ids.
criteria.B: Option B: per-vertex numeric channels in the existing timeline.
criteria.C: Option C: no path animation, morph effect only.

hold_on_topology_change.instructions: When two neighbouring path keys have different vertex ids or a different open or closed state, should the engine hold the earlier key rather than interpolate by vertex index?

criteria.true: Yes: hold the earlier key and say so by name; interpolating by index silently distorts the shape.
criteria.false: No: interpolate by index anyway so something always moves.

gpu_refuse_until_redraw.instructions: Is it acceptable to land path animation first on the contract, the evaluator, the CPU reference and the Editor, and have the GPU engine refuse an animated path by name until per-frame source redraw is built, as it already does for animated width and height?

criteria.true: Yes: ship in verified steps and refuse by name rather than render it wrongly.
criteria.false: No: nothing may land until the GPU renders it too.

ids_on_the_path.instructions: Should every vertex carry a stable id stored on the path itself (an optional list parallel to the vertices, absent on old scenes), rather than correspondence by vertex index?

criteria.true: Yes: ids on the path survive inserts, deletes, reorders and undo, and keep old scenes valid.
criteria.false: No: correspondence by index is enough.
